status: proposed by Claude on 2026-11-23 from the design-decision table (written before the step-3 rules); needs sign-off by Moomal and Rama

categories.A: one supported plan: all required facts known, one rule applies
categories.B: several valid plans; a documented choice rule picks one
categories.C: needs review: a required fact is missing, or the program's behaviour conflicts with Rust ownership

01.why: local file, defer always registered, no escape

02.why: early return before the defer: guard never created on that path

03.why: early return after the defer: guard drops on that path too

04.why: acquisition fails on every tested input; the plan for the success path is still a guard

05.why: two guards declared in acquisition order; Rust drops them in reverse (LIFO)

06.why: guard hoisted to function scope: Go closes at function exit, not block exit

07.why: defer registered on one branch only

08.why: defer in a loop: explicit stack popped in reverse (a Vec drops first-to-last)

09.why: returned open; the caller owns and closes it

10.why: returns a handle its own defer already closed; the caller uses it after close

11.why: ownership moves into a global; main closes it

12.why: the alias is a borrow of the same file

13.why: defer argument fixed at registration (A); B closed explicitly

14.why: deferred closure reads a reassigned variable at exit

15.why: closure parameter fixed at registration (A); B closed explicitly

16.why: closes the same file twice; the named result depends on the second close failing

17.why: guard drops during unwinding; recover needs catch_unwind

18.why: the helper's defer closes the caller's file, then the caller uses it

19.why: explicit close followed by a deferred close of the same file

20.why: deferred interface call with one possible implementation
